relevant_clauses.text: This privacy policy (the “Privacy Policy”), together with our Terms & Conditions at ada.com/terms-and-conditions, our Cookie Policy at ada.com/cookie-policy and any other documents referred therein, sets out the basis on which any personal data we collect from you, or that you provide to us, will be processed. Please read this Privacy Policy carefully to understand the types of data we collect from you, how we use it, the circumstances under which we will share it with third parties, and your rights in relation to your personal data.

This Privacy Policy applies to any personal data processed by Ada Health GmbH (HRB 189710), Neue Grünstraße 17, 10179 Berlin, Germany being the data controller (as defined under Article 4(7) GDPR) of all processing activities in connection with the Services. Questions, comments and requests regarding this Privacy Policy are welcome and should be addressed via email to support@ada.com or through our contact form here. Our data protection officer can be contacted at dpo@ada.com.

Before starting using our Services, you should read our Privacy Policy carefully. In order to use our Symptom Assessment and other health related features, you have to consent to Ada analyzing the personal health data you voluntarily share in order to be provided with an assessment and health advice.

analysis.justification: The policy clearly identifies the data controller and provides contact details for inquiries, fulfilling the transparency requirement under Article 5(1)(a) by using clear and plain language as emphasized in Recital 39. It systematically details each processing activity in section 3 with specific legal bases, purposes, and data types, ensuring lawfulness and fairness through explicit consent for health data and legitimate interests where appropriate, aligning with Recital 39's call for transparent processing. The inclusion of data subject rights and safeguards for international transfers further supports compliance with EDPB guidelines on transparency.

analysis.article_5_text: collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner that is incompatible with those purposes; further processing for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes shall, in accordance with Article 89(1), not be considered to be incompatible with the initial purposes (‘purpose limitation’);
analysis.recital_39_reference: “Specific purposes... explicit and legitimate and determined at the time of the collection.”

relevant_clauses.text: This privacy policy ... sets out the basis on which any personal data we collect from you, or that you provide to us, will be processed.
This section 2 aims at giving you a quick high-level overview of the data processing activities in connection with the Services we provide you.
Which personal data we may collect and process, why and for how long

Purpose of processing: We use the above data to provide you with access to our Services, to ensure that the Services can establish an internet connection smoothly and are easy to use. We also use this data to analyze the system security and stability, as well as for additional administrative purposes.
Purpose of processing: We use the above data to provide you with a user account and access to our App. We use the general health data for the basic analysis.

Purpose of processing: We use the above data to enable the use of Ada Assess on our website or in the infrastructure of our business partners (website, app or other platform) and facilitate the exchange of data between Ada and the business partner.
Purpose of processing: This feature allows you to provide additional health information about you and create a comprehensive health profile to manage your health data in our App.

Purpose of processing: If you choose to login using a third party login feature from either Apple. Facebook or Google, we will receive the data listed above from the third-party provider with your approval to populate your user data in the App, and to verify your identity.
Purpose of processing: When you use the different features of the App or Ada Assess we process your data including your health data to provide you with the requested functionality.

Purpose of processing: Certain options to address the identified causes may be provided by our partners, such as branded medication or informational materials. When you select to view these partner options, we show you available options based on the determined conditions in your assessment report as possible next steps.

Purpose of processing: When you allow us to invite you to research projects, we might contact you and suggest participating in specific projects that are either carried out by us or by our research partners.
Purpose of processing: We process pseudonymized data to carry out aggregate statistics on the results of the symptom assessments conducted by our users.

Purpose of processing: We process pseudonymized data for public health purposes (as defined by GDPR recital 54) such as analyzing case data regarding public health trends, rare diseases and threats, and to identify factors that could improve public health...

Purpose of processing: To guarantee high quality and safety standards of our medical devices, i.e., the Ada Health App and Ada Assess, it is necessary to systematically monitor their quality, performance and safety (“Post-Market-Surveillance”).
Purpose of processing: We process some usage data (which does not include personal health data) if you are using the App, to understand how Ada reaches people online.
Purpose of processing: Ada implements a variety of technical and organisational measures to ensure that your data is adequately protected.
Purpose of processing: We process you data to send you direct marketing (products and services) or communication about any survey that we believe will be of interest to you.
Purpose of processing: We use a limited set of usage data (which does not include personal health data) to track your page interaction and analyze the data to optimize our marketing initiatives.

Purpose of processing: We use the above data (which does not include personal health data) to ensure the proper use, functioning, maintenance and improvement of our Services (our Services cannot function properly without this processing) as well as to prevent any decompiling or otherwise reverse engineering.
Purpose of processing: Ada is relying on feedback and surveys in various scenarios to understand if and how our products can be improved to match your needs.
Purpose of processing: Based on your consent, we can contact you via push notifications in the Ada app to help you make the best use of Ada’s functionalities.

Purpose of processing: We will use data that we have stored about you to the extent that this is necessary to exercise a legal claim of our own or to defend us against a legal claim you file against us.

Purpose of processing: Ada will share your data with a government entities such as a law enforcement agencies to the extent that it is necessary to prevent harm to others and to yourself or required by applicable law or required to comply with a valid court order, subpoena, search warrant or other order by a competent authority.

We are developing new technological capabilities (e.g. Artificial Intelligence/Large Language Models) to improve our product performance and user experience. For the validation of such capabilities we only use anonymized real world user data such as anonymized past assessment data.

If your personal data is used for more than one purpose, we will retain it until the purpose with the longest period expires, but we will stop using it for the purpose with the shorter period as soon as the shorter period expires (to comply with the purpose limitation principle).

analysis.justification: The policy explicitly specifies purposes for each data processing activity in section 3, such as providing symptom assessments or conducting post-market surveillance, meeting Article 5(1)(b)'s requirement for explicit and legitimate purposes determined at collection as per Recital 39. It ensures no incompatible further processing by limiting uses to stated purposes and anonymizing data for research or statistics, consistent with Article 89(1) exceptions. The commitment to stop using data for shorter-period purposes when they expire directly supports purpose limitation under EDPB guidelines on data protection by design.

analysis.article_5_text: adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed (‘data minimisation’);
analysis.recital_39_reference: “Adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary... processed only if... could not reasonably be fulfilled by other means.”

analysis.justification: The policy lists specific, limited data types for each purpose in section 3, such as only collecting health symptoms necessary for assessments, aligning with Article 5(1)(c)'s requirement to limit data to what is necessary as per Recital 39. It emphasizes optional data fields and warns that non-provision may limit functionality, ensuring data is adequate and relevant without excess, consistent with EDPB Guidelines 4/2019 on data protection by design. Anonymization for research and pseudonymization where possible further minimize personal data processing, fulfilling the principle that data should only be processed if purposes cannot be achieved otherwise.

analysis.article_5_text: accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date; every reasonable step must be taken to ensure that personal data that are inaccurate, having regard to the purposes for which they are processed, are erased or rectified without delay (‘accuracy’);
analysis.recital_39_reference: “Every reasonable step should be taken to ensure that personal data which are inaccurate are rectified or deleted.”

relevant_clauses.text: When you update information such as height and weight in your profile, we will keep the previous entries to allow you to track its development.

You may revoke/withdraw your consent at any time; however, it is not possible to provide you with our symptom assessment or other health related features without such consent, as they rely on the processing of your health data.

Such a review can be prompted by your medically relevant feedback or a lodged complaint. If you voluntarily share findings of your medical treatment we will use this information for purposes of Post-Market-Surveillance as well.

Right to Rectification: As a data subject, you have the right to rectification under the conditions provided in Article 16 GDPR. This means in particular that you have the right to receive from us, without undue delay, the rectification of inaccuracies in your personal data and completion of incomplete personal data.

analysis.justification: The policy enables users to update profiles and provides a right to rectification under Article 16, linking to Article 5(1)(d) by allowing prompt correction of inaccuracies as required by Recital 39. However, it lacks explicit mechanisms for verifying or ensuring the accuracy of health data inputted by users, which is critical for medical assessments, potentially failing to take every reasonable step for rectification or deletion. While feedback integration in post-market surveillance supports accuracy reviews, the absence of proactive measures like data validation aligns partially with EDPB guidelines on transparency but does not fully demonstrate comprehensive accuracy controls.

analysis.article_5_text: kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed; personal data may be stored for longer periods insofar as the personal data will be processed solely for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes in accordance with Article 89(1) subject to implementation of the appropriate technical and organisational measures required by this Regulation in order to safeguard the rights and freedoms of the data subject (‘storage limitation’);
analysis.recital_39_reference: “Period... stored is limited to a strict minimum... time limits... for erasure or... periodic review.”

If a security-relevant event occurs, log files of the servers are stored until the security-relevant event has been completely eliminated and clarified.

Storage duration: Your data will be stored until it is no longer required for the survey for which it was collected. ... Where possible we will anonymize any information that might identify you during the evaluation for further processing.
Storage duration: Your data will be stored until it is no longer required for the purpose for which it was collected, or you revoke your consent.

Storage duration: Your data is being processed for litigation purposes as long as your account is still active. After termination of the account, we will retain your data for up to seven years in secured form as described above.

Storage duration: Your data will be transferred to the competent authorities and stored by them as controllers according to applicable retention periods. Ada will store the documentation of the data transfer for up to four years following the sharing of data.

We will hold your personal data for as long as it is necessary or required by law or by any relevant regulatory body, and always in compliance with the data minimization principle. ... If your personal data is used for more than one purpose, we will retain it until the purpose with the longest period expires... After the processing of your data is no longer necessary for the purposes outlined in section 3 or your account is deleted (see section 3.2) we will securely and separately store some of your data in accordance with statutory retention obligations applicable to us and reasonable business needs. We will retain Post-Market-Surveillance data (incl. health data) in accordance with our storage obligations according to the medical device law. We will retain data (incl. health data) in relation to your use of our Services for up to seven years in accordance with our business needs for the purposes of establishing, exercising or defending against legal claims. ... If the processing of your personal data is no longer necessary for any purpose it is either irreversibly anonymized (and the anonymized data may be retained), or securely erased.

analysis.justification: The policy specifies time-limited retention periods for each processing activity in section 3, such as 15 days for access logs or until account deletion for user profiles, satisfying Article 5(1)(e)'s requirement for storage no longer than necessary as per Recital 39's strict minimum. It allows longer storage for public interest purposes like research with anonymization safeguards, aligning with Article 89(1) exceptions. Provisions for periodic review through deletion requests and secure vaulting for legal claims demonstrate compliance with EDPB guidelines on data protection by default.

analysis.article_5_text: processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security of the personal data, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage, using appropriate technical or organisational measures (‘integrity and confidentiality’);
analysis.recital_39_reference: “Processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security and confidentiality... preventing unauthorised access.”

relevant_clauses.text: For Ada Health GmbH (“Ada”, “us”, “our” or “we”) it is vitally important that our customers (the “users”) feel secure when using our products and services.

Ada implements a variety of technical and organisational measures to ensure that your data is adequately protected. The implementation of these measures is expressly required by law in Art. 32 GDPR and is also needed for the ISO 27001 certification of Ada's information security management system. ... Your data can only be accessed by limited personal subject to a procedure that involves approval by our Data Processing Officer.

The personal data that we collect from you is stored in the European Union on Cloud Servers of Amazon Web Services EMEA S.A.R.L. (“AWS”) ... Sensitive information between your browser and our Website is transferred in encrypted form using Transport Layer Security (“TLS”). When transmitting sensitive information, you should always make sure that your browser can validate our certificate.

We use technical service providers to operate and maintain our Services, who act as our processors based on data processing agreements as required by Art. 28 GDPR. ... Where we use Service providers who process personal data on our behalf outside the EEA (or “third countries”) we do so with the appropriate safeguards for your data subject rights. Most of our US service providers are certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. Where this is not the case, we have agreed on the Standard Contractual Clauses with added securities (where necessary).

We restrict access to your personal data to the persons who need to use it for the relevant purpose(s), always in compliance with the integrity and confidentiality principle. After the processing of your data is no longer necessary ... we will securely and separately store some of your data in accordance with statutory retention obligations applicable to us and reasonable business needs.

analysis.justification: The policy describes technical measures like TLS encryption, ISO 27001 certification, and bug bounty programs, directly addressing Article 5(1)(f)'s security requirements against unauthorized access as per Recital 39. It mandates data processing agreements under Article 28 GDPR for processors and uses EU-US Data Privacy Framework or SCCs for transfers, ensuring confidentiality. The restricted access and encrypted vaulting for retained data align with EDPB Guidelines 4/2019 on implementing appropriate organizational measures for integrity and confidentiality.

analysis.justification: The policy demonstrates accountability under Article 5(2) by appointing a DPO with contact details and maintaining ISO 27001 certification for security management. It evidences compliance through data processing agreements with processors and explicit references to adhering to principles like minimization and purpose limitation. The detailed facilitation of data subject rights and change notification procedures further show responsibility, aligning with EDPB guidelines on transparency and data protection by design.
